attrs.evidence: Falls out of EMB-REVOKE-IRREVERSIBLE and is the question that record hands forward. The reversibility TYPE of a hereditary capability is decided by where its kernel sits: an internalized kernel makes heredity irreversible, an externalized-and-gated one makes it revocable by withdrawal. If the location is a choice, then a factory can buy revocability at externalization time by paying for a dependency — which is a design lever nobody in either Mosaic proposal has named. If it is a property of the capability, it is a constraint and the factory must plan around it.
attrs.prior_art: EMB-KERNEL (Fable, embodiment program): the minimal persistent artifact set that lets a compatible replacement substrate retain c. This record asks where that set is allowed to live, which the original did not.
attrs.statement: For a capability c, does its continuity kernel live inside the descendant (internalized) or behind an artifact the parent still controls (externalized and gated) — and is that a property of c, or a choice made at externalization time?
